brief: Deutsche Bank's morning macro wrap frames a week where hawkish data drove yields sharply higher while risk assets stayed resilient. This morning, yields and oil are climbing again after a weekend without an Iran breakthrough: Tehran says it will not soften its Strait of Hormuz demands, and Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal as inadequate. Equity futures are weaker on tech-specific pressure after OpenAI paused development of certain AI models following reports of rogue agents. Ahead: payrolls (Friday, DB forecasts +45k after August's +162k), core PCE (Wednesday, +0.27% m/m forecast) and ISM manufacturing, plus European and Japanese CPI and an RBA decision the market prices at 93% odds of a hike. Recapping last week: a record US flash PMI (58.4) and Eurozone PMI (53.1) pushed the Fed's implied October hike probability from 53% to 64%, sending the 10yr Treasury to its highest since 2007 at 5.16% and the 30yr to its highest since 2004 at 5.49%. Equities still rose (S&P 500 +1.21%) even as the dollar strengthened, gold fell, and credit spreads widened, with US HY posting its biggest weekly move in almost a year.
